nodes.label: Two kinds of extraction
nodes.source_location: Two kinds of extraction, and which needs what
nodes.rationale: Code is parsed by tree-sitter AST, free and fully local with no model involved, and runs on the post-commit hook. Docs, PDFs and images need a model and run through /graphify . inside Claude Code on the existing subscription, with no API key on the integration machine. The semantic pass is what makes the graph useful rather than merely structural.

nodes.label: Union merge driver for graph.json
nodes.rationale: graph.json is regenerated on every commit, so two people committing in the same week always touch it. Git will not use a merge driver it has not been told about and that registration is per-clone config the repository cannot carry, so `make graph-setup` registers it once. Without it you get an ordinary conflict in a 300 KB generated file, which must never be hand-merged: take either side and rebuild. `-diff linguist-generated` keeps the graph out of PR diffs.

nodes.label: Amend the graph refresh into the commit
nodes.source_location: The hook leaves your tree dirty
nodes.rationale: The post-commit hook rebuilds after the commit lands, leaving graphify-out/ dirty. Fold it back with `git commit --amend --no-edit -- graphify-out/` so the graph in a commit describes that commit. Leaving it for the next commit means every feature commit carries somebody else's graph refresh, which is what makes a graph commit unreviewable. Never amend a commit already pushed.

nodes.label: Domain pack
nodes.rationale: The core platform knows nothing about tax or insurance - only how to ingest, search and answer with a citation. A pack is one YAML file that teaches it a subject, declaring document types and fields, a grounding corpus, capability-module registrations, a persona and guardrails. Since ADR 0017 document types and fields moved to core/documents.yaml and a pack holds only grounding, persona, guardrails, answering rules and advice.

nodes.label: A field name is three things at once
nodes.source_location: 2. The one thing to understand before you start
nodes.rationale: A field name becomes the extraction model's attribute, the facts.key it is stored under, and the column header in the corpus register. If the field is pay_period and the register column says period, nothing errors - the evaluation silently scores zero on that field and it is found in week 8. So register headers are generated from the pack, which makes field lists a week-1 dependency rather than a week-3 one.
nodes.norm_label: a field name is three things at once

nodes.label: The ten field types
nodes.rationale: string, identifier, person, money, integer, percent, date, month, enum, boolean. Each names its storage column (value_text, value_num, value_date) and its exact register format, so the spreadsheet and the database agree on what a value looks like. Pick by what the value is, not by how it is printed.

nodes.label: identifier versus string
nodes.rationale: An identifier is matched exactly and never cleaned up - no spaces removed, no case changed - because MV-2026-448120 and mv2026448120 are different policies as far as a claim is concerned. This is the distinction that matters most among the ten types.

nodes.label: Five to eight fields per document type
nodes.rationale: Twelve is the hard limit. A field earns its place by being used by a module or by answering a plausible question. Every extra field is one the corpus owner fills in for hundreds of documents and one the extractor can get wrong, so breadth costs accuracy twice. required: false for fields a real document sometimes omits - a missing required field quarantines the whole document, which is right for a policy number and wrong for an optional excess.
nodes.norm_label: five to eight fields per document type

nodes.label: Pack guardrails
nodes.rationale: must_cite (no claim without a document and page), abstain_below (the retrieval score under which the system says it does not know), never_acts (cannot be set to false - the type system rejects it), and the disclaimer rendered under every answer. Insurance sits at 0.45 and tax at 0.42 because a wrong answer about cover is worse than an unhelpful one. Regulatory framing belongs in the disclaimer, not the persona.

nodes.label: Pack persona is voice only
nodes.rationale: It cannot change retrieval, the score floor or the guardrails, so behaviour must not be smuggled into it. Two or three sentences on what the assistant does and, importantly, what it does not do.

nodes.label: Pack grounding corpus
nodes.rationale: Authoritative reference material indexed beside the user's own documents. Never paraphrase a rule into it - index what the publisher wrote, because the moment you summarise the assistant cites your summary as though it were the publisher. Version by what the guidance applies to (iras_reliefs_ya2026, not iras_reliefs_september). Every file needs a sources.yaml provenance entry. A pack with no corpus is fine and sometimes correct.

nodes.label: Registering with capability modules
nodes.rationale: A pack declares reminder entries (from_field naming a date field, lead_days) and alert entries (metric, ceiling, warn_at) and gets reminders and alerts without writing any logic. Registering a module that is not installed is ignored rather than an error, so declaring a future module is safe.

nodes.label: python -m packs.build
nodes.rationale: Regenerates core/document_schemas.py (the decode constraint on the extraction model), corpus/register/core_columns.csv and the batch template (the register header row), and docs/field-dictionary.md. All three are committed alongside the source. CI fails if a pack is edited and the generated files are not regenerated - deliberately.

nodes.label: START.cmd launcher
nodes.rationale: One double-click starts three things that fail independently - the engine on 127.0.0.1:8000, the Next.js screens on 3000, and the ingestion worker (plus Telegram capture when a token is configured). The one a person is looking at always comes up. The engine passes its real port to the screens so PARROT_API_URL no longer has to be kept in step by hand. Windows-only; macOS has preflight but no double-click launcher.

nodes.label: The watched inbox folder
nodes.rationale: The SHA-256 of the bytes is the document's identity, so the same file renamed, re-downloaded or sent through a second channel is recognised as the document it already is. A file is registered a few seconds after it stops changing, never while still being written, and in-progress names (.part, .crdownload, .tmp, leading . or ~$) are skipped.

nodes.label: Quarantine and the vision second pass
nodes.rationale: A document the parser could not read queues rather than being dropped. --retry renders its pages and sends them to the vision-language model, which reads pixels rather than recovered text, then holds the result to the same pack schema and reports a recovery rate. Retry matches rows to files by SHA-256, so the original must still be in the inbox; a document whose file has left is offered as Forget it instead.
nodes.norm_label: quarantine and the vision second pass

nodes.label: Dense-only retrieval stopgap
nodes.source_location: Current build stage; Asking a question
nodes.rationale: scripts/ask.py and api/routes.py import DenseRetriever and NoReranker from core/graph/baseline.py. Answer quality is therefore not a number anybody should quote: the mechanism works, the ranking is naive on purpose, and the numbers come from the evaluation harness against a golden set.

nodes.label: Rebuilding the vault's vectors
nodes.source_location: After a change to chunking or embedding
nodes.rationale: scripts/reindex.py re-parses, re-chunks and re-embeds each indexed document and leaves facts, obligations and corrections alone. A vault embedded the old way is not searchable the new way - queries and passages must be embedded alike - so questions answer badly until it has run.

nodes.label: Telegram capture
nodes.rationale: Long polling, not a webhook: the laptop makes a request out, nothing listens on a public port, no tunnel. Media is written into the inbox, registered, read, then deleted at source so Telegram keeps no copy on the household's behalf. The allow list is configuration rather than a command-line flag because a list that lives only in a command line is one a double-click cannot honour.

nodes.label: The ingestion worker
nodes.rationale: The watcher registers and queues; scripts/worker.py reads. The setup page separates two failures that look alike - 'Queue broker' is whether Redis answers, 'Ingestion worker' is whether anything listens to it, because a reachable broker with no worker means documents register, queue and sit there looking filed while nothing reads them. On Windows the pool is solo and --beat is a second process.

nodes.label: Startup integration contract
nodes.rationale: /healthz means the diagnostic API is alive. /readyz is hardcoded to HTTP 503 with stage: setup and does not turn true when the screens run, because this server supervises the engine and worker and never the Next.js process - it is in no position to declare the product ready. No runtime implementation should mark the app ready merely because a port responds.

nodes.label: Score against the register, never against a facts table
nodes.source_location: Three things that decide whether two people's numbers are comparable
nodes.rationale: Extraction is a model call, not a pure function: temperature 0.0 with no seed is near-deterministic for one model and quantisation and is not guaranteed identical across GPUs and drivers. Two people can hold different facts rows for the same document, and only corpus/register/*.csv is the same on both machines - which is why evaluation never reads a live database for an expected answer. Record the models and quantisation too, because a different pull is a different vector space.
nodes.norm_label: score against the register, never against a facts table

nodes.label: The redacted real-document holdout
nodes.rationale: corpus/holdout/ is 40 real, redacted documents from team members - personal data under the consent and redaction protocol, gitignored, never committed, scored once in week 8 and never used for tuning. It is different in kind from a synthetic batch and does not travel on the same terms. The database is a derived artifact; nobody ships one.

nodes.label: Hardware qualification
nodes.rationale: Minimum specifications are unconfirmed; the 8 GB GPU claim is a planning estimate, not a supported-device guarantee, and a successful startup check is not a benchmark. The external RTX 3080 is build-only and the onboard RTX 4060 is the demo baseline - results using the 3080 cannot be presented as 4060 results. Model presence is not validation of generation, vision, embeddings or reranking.

nodes.author: Christian
nodes.rationale: The person who owns the contracts owns the platform. Deliberately the lane with the least new feature code, because an integrator who is also mid-feature stops integrating. Owns core/contracts.py, db/migrations/, core/graph/, core/adapters/, core/ingest/ orchestration, modules/, the repo and the merge queue.

nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Owns core/retrieve/, parsing and chunking config, embeddings, the reranker, the abstain floor and eval/. The seam is deliberate: this lane owns the measurement of extraction quality while Lane A owns the extraction engine, because the person who built a thing should not be the only person scoring it.

nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: Not a documentation role. Six artefacts, each a chapter of the report: data inventory, retention and erasure policy, model card, ISO/IEC 22989-to-5338 map, IMDA GenAI nine-dimension mapping, autonomy statement - plus the consent and redaction protocol that makes the holdout corpus lawful to collect, and the 15-item adversarial Set C.

nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: Both halves are content-shaped work that AI coding tools handle well: a pack is mostly YAML, a schema and a grounding corpus; the interface is generated against a finished design pack. Owns packs/iras_tax/, packs/insurance_agent/ and web/, and the four surfaces Today, Ask, Vault and Packs.
nodes.norm_label: lane d - domain packs and interface

nodes.label: Lane E - Corpus and adversarial testing
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: The corpus is the input to every other lane, so it starts in week 1 and never blocks. Owns the household canon, the register, all templates, every batch and the quarantine review. The pairing with adversarial testing is the same instinct twice: knowing what a real document looks like, and knowing how someone would try to get around a control.
nodes.norm_label: lane e - corpus and adversarial testing

nodes.label: Fill the register first
nodes.source_location: The one process change that matters
nodes.rationale: Do not generate documents and then work out what is in them. Canon, then register, then one template per type, then mail merge, then print and photograph a subset. Filling the register first gives extraction F1 measured directly rather than by hand-labelling 400 documents in week 8, most of golden Set A generated rather than written, internal consistency across documents, and mass production without code.

nodes.label: Contracts before code
nodes.rationale: With three builders and their agents on one repository the failure mode is not slow progress, it is five plausible-looking implementations of the same idea. core/contracts.py and the schema land in week 1 in their own reviewed PRs: an agent given a schema is consistent across sessions and people, an agent given prose is not. Nobody edits core/contracts.py in a feature PR - a contract quietly widened to make one feature easier is how a multi-agent repository degrades.

nodes.label: Say what synthetic data does not prove
nodes.rationale: Generated documents are cleaner and more consistent than real ones, so a score measured only on them overstates the system. That is what the 40-document holdout is for: report both numbers and the gap, because the gap is a finding, not a defect. The invented-organisations rule was withdrawn on 13 September 2026 - real hospitals, schemes and dispute bodies may be named where a real document would name them.
nodes.norm_label: say what synthetic data does not prove

nodes.label: The demonstration run sheet
nodes.author: Christian
nodes.rationale: Nine steps in 7:50, leaving room to lose twenty seconds and still land under eight minutes. Ordered so any single step can be dropped without breaking the one after it - except the abstention, which is why it sits fifth from the end rather than last. The demonstration fails in the ten minutes before it starts, not during it, so the checklist is run on the presenting machine.

nodes.label: Step 6 - the abstention
nodes.rationale: The step the demonstration exists for. Neither installed pack covers utilities, so asking for an electricity bill makes the abstention structural rather than lucky and it survives a corpus change. A system like this is useful not because it answers but because you can believe the answers, and you can only believe them if it is willing to say no. The headline evaluation number is the abstention rate on questions the corpus genuinely cannot answer.

nodes.label: Step 7 - the refusal to act
nodes.rationale: It refuses at the top of the graph, before retrieval runs - it did not go and look and then decline. Every pack manifest declares never_acts: true and the type system accepts no other value, so a pack that says otherwise does not load. A boundary that can be pointed at in the code rather than a promise about the model's judgement.

nodes.label: Step 8 - switch a pack off
nodes.rationale: The platform argument as one gesture: reminders disappear, the documents are hidden from the vault, Ask abstains on a question it could answer a moment ago, and nothing is deleted. Nothing in the engine changed - the registry is read once per request and handed to the modules and to retrieval, neither of which knows a screen exists. A third subject appears because somebody dropped a YAML file in, not because anybody edited the interface.

nodes.label: Step 2 - the source chip
nodes.rationale: Every row names the document and page it came from and pressing it shows that page, with the row still behind it - checking a claim does not cost you the claim. If the panel says the file is not in the inbox any more, that is correct honest behaviour, not a crash.

nodes.label: The correctly-cited wrong person
nodes.rationale: The only failure mode in the architecture that citation does not defend against. Two term life policies differing only in whose name is on them both match; a cross-encoder has no representation of which human being a document is about, so it orders by textual relevance; the gate checks the sentence is supported by a retrieved chunk, and it is. The answer is delivered with a correct citation to the wrong person's policy and every check passes. The word 'my' had nothing to bind to.

nodes.label: Derive the roster, then confirm it
nodes.source_location: 3 - Why a roster is not a setup form
nodes.rationale: facts.subject is a printed string, so matching is about which strings a household's documents actually use, not about knowing who lives in the house. A person filling a first-run roster works from memory before any document is filed and produces something that looks complete and matches nothing - the worst state, because it is indistinguishable from a working one until an answer is wrong. So setup asks one question, everybody else arrives off a document, a person confirms, and only confirmed aliases scope anything. A wrong guess costs a tap, which is why the generator is allowed to guess.
nodes.norm_label: derive the roster, then confirm it

nodes.label: people and person_aliases
nodes.rationale: Two tables in db/migrations/0002_household.sql plus telegram_identities and document_attribution for provenance. An alias carries the literal string a document printed, its source (setup, model, user), whether it is confirmed, the generator's confidence and the document that raised the question. Attribution is the only ownership signal arriving before parsing - a payslip photographed on Rachel's phone is Rachel's whatever the OCR makes of the name - and a disagreement with extraction becomes a question rather than a silent overwrite.

nodes.label: facts.subject is never normalised
nodes.rationale: The alias table sits beside facts.subject and maps it; what the page said stays what the page said, so correcting the roster later cannot retroactively edit the record of what a document claimed. This mirrors the existing rule that identifier fields are stored verbatim. Matching is on lower(btrim(...)) only.

nodes.label: Exactly one owner, enforced by the database
nodes.rationale: A partial unique index (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX ... WHERE is_owner) rather than application code. 'Who is me' is the predicate every first-person answer is scoped by, and two of them is not a state any screen knows how to render, so the database refuses it. The owner is a row rather than a config value because households are handed over, and an install that cannot follow that gets abandoned rather than corrected.
nodes.norm_label: exactly one owner, enforced by the database

nodes.label: Three buckets, not two
nodes.rationale: core/graph/scope.py partitions retrieved passages into mine (keep), someone else's (drop) and the household's, where subject IS NULL (keep). The third bucket is the one an implementation forgets: a home contents policy names nobody because it belongs to the address, and excluding it would break 'my home insurance' while looking like an empty vault. First-person detection is deliberately conservative - a relationship word or a non-owner's name leaves the question unscoped, because an over-eager filter fails as an absence rather than as an error.

nodes.label: Scoping happens after retrieval, and that has a ceiling
nodes.source_location: 7 - What this cost, and what it did not
nodes.rationale: core/contracts.py was not touched (a household is not a pack and not a module) and neither was core/graph/ports.py, the contract with Lane B - which is why scoping happens after retrieval rather than as a SQL predicate. The measurable cost: a passage that did not survive the candidate cut cannot be scoped back in. With CANDIDATES = 40 over a household vault this is not currently reachable, but it is a real ceiling to hand to Lane B when hybrid search lands, because pushing the predicate into the query is a retrieval change and belongs with a retrieval measurement.
nodes.norm_label: scoping happens after retrieval, and that has a ceiling

nodes.label: The Lim household canon
nodes.rationale: Five people with fixed roles, ID numbers, dates of birth and employers: Marcus Lim Jun Wei (owner), Rachel Ng Hui Shan (partner), Lucas Lim Kai En (child), Lim Ah Kow and Tan Mei Ling (parents), one canonical address, two approved insurers and one financing bank. Every generated document must agree with it, which is what makes cross-document consistency free.

nodes.label: Republic of Xinkapow
nodes.rationale: An invented jurisdiction with a deliberately non-Singaporean visual identity - yellow and orange guilloche, a mascot crest replacing any national coat of arms - so that generated identity documents cannot be mistaken for, or resemble, real national identity cards.

nodes.label: Synthetic specimen watermark
nodes.rationale: 'PROJECT PARROT - SYNTHETIC SPECIMEN - FOR RESEARCH EVALUATION ONLY' is written into every image-generation prompt as a diagonal translucent stamp across the card face, so the marking is part of the generated pixels rather than metadata that a screenshot would strip.

nodes.label: Gemini prompt bank for identity specimens
nodes.rationale: Eight reusable prompts producing photorealistic identity cards, a birth certificate and a passport data page, each restating the canon's ID numbers and dates verbatim so the image's printed values are ground truth rather than whatever the generator invented.
nodes.norm_label: gemini prompt bank for identity specimens

nodes.label: Ground truth Q&A test matrix
nodes.rationale: Ten questions paired with the exact answer and the document, page or clause that must be cited - including two designed to fail safely: the passport question that must abstain until the image exists, and the term life premium question that must disambiguate Marcus from Rachel per ADR 0011.

nodes.label: ADR 0001 - Record architecture decisions
nodes.rationale: Undocumented choices get re-litigated, and an agent with no record of a decision will cheerfully make a different one next session. An ADR is half a page recording what was chosen, what was rejected and why - not how to implement it. The report's technical chapter is largely assembled from them, and writing them as we go is cheaper than reconstructing them in November.

nodes.label: ADR 0002 - One PostgreSQL instance for everything
nodes.rationale: The questions a household assistant answers are relational selects and aggregates, not graph traversals, and generated Cypher from a quantised local model is the highest-variance component that could sit on a live demo path. PostgreSQL 17 with pgvector holds chunks (dense plus tsvector lexical), typed facts, obligations, LangGraph state and the registry. ChromaDB was rejected for having no keyword search; a separate graph database for being a second query language and a second failure mode for no gain. It is also the stack with the deepest representation in training data, which matters when agents write most of the code.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0002 - one postgresql instance for everything

nodes.label: Reciprocal rank fusion of dense and lexical
nodes.rationale: Retrieval fuses the dense (pgvector cosine) and lexical (tsvector) rankings with RRF. Module queries are hand-written and parameterised; nothing generates SQL at runtime.
nodes.norm_label: reciprocal rank fusion of dense and lexical

nodes.label: ADR 0003 - PaperBrain informs the pattern, not the module
nodes.rationale: core/retrieve/ ports PaperBrain's retrieval pattern - hybrid BM25 plus dense fused with RRF, hash-based idempotent ingest, per-page OCR fallback, a refuse-to-guess grounded prompt - rebuilt against Postgres, Docling and the pinned models. Adopting it wholesale would violate ADR 0002 with a second datastore, swap in unpinned models, ship no reranker and no graph, and pull in a parallel dependency set. Designing from a blank page would throw away a validated design. The cost: PaperBrain now needs someone to keep it from silently diverging as a second unmaintained implementation.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0003 - paperbrain informs the pattern, not the module

nodes.label: PaperBrain prototype
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: A working local-RAG prototype in tools/paperbrain/: SQLite plus FTS5 plus numpy cosine, pypdf and Tesseract for parsing, nomic-embed-text and qwen2.5:14b-instruct, no orchestration graph, built for a 64 GB unified-memory Mac. It stays where it is, unmodified, as a reference implementation.

nodes.label: ADR 0004 - Local setup can run before the assistant is ready
nodes.rationale: A missing database or model must be understandable to nontechnical teammates without claiming the unfinished assistant works. The launcher starts a loopback-only FastAPI diagnostic server that owns its socket, refuses a busy port and opens the browser only once started; /readyz returns 503 throughout the setup stage. It never installs dependencies, downloads models, applies migrations or processes household documents. Model metadata is not proof that inference works, and the base-table check is schema presence, not migration integrity.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0004 - local setup can run before the assistant is ready

nodes.label: ADR 0005 - The watched folder is polled, not subscribed to
nodes.rationale: A filesystem event is the wrong signal: a file is created at the start of a copy, not the end, so anything built on watchdog events still has to debounce by watching the file stop changing - the event stream only decides how often we look. On Windows ReadDirectoryChangesW also drops events under buffer pressure, which would mean a document silently never filed. Adding a runtime dependency for one directory holding a handful of files a week also fails AGENTS.md rule 5.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0005 - the watched folder is polled, not subscribed to

nodes.label: Stability debounce with injected time
nodes.rationale: A file is ready when size and mtime are unchanged for stable_seconds (3.0) across polls poll_seconds apart (1.0) and it is not empty - roughly four seconds after a copy finishes, never a half-written file. Elapsed time is passed into FolderAdapter.observe(elapsed) rather than read from a clock inside it, so the debounce is tested without any test sleeping. The already-filed memory is in-process, so a restart re-hashes files still in the inbox; the register upsert makes that costless but noisy.

nodes.label: ADR 0006 - pypdfium2 renders the quarantine page images
nodes.rationale: Asking Docling for the page images would mean asking the component that could not read the document to prepare the evidence for the component that might, making the recovery rate a measurement of Docling twice. Shelling out to pdftoppm trades a declared dependency for an undeclared system one. pypdfium2 was already present transitively via Docling; declaring it directly is the point - code we call is a dependency we own, and a transitive dependency dropped in a minor release must break a lock file rather than break quarantine silently. 150 dpi is legible for 8pt print; four pages is a household document.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0006 - pypdfium2 renders the quarantine page images

nodes.label: ADR 0007 - The graph ships before retrieval and before a checkpoint table
nodes.rationale: Writing a retriever in core/retrieve/ would put two people's agents in the same directory in the same week and produce a second unmeasured baseline beside the one Lane B must publish. PostgresSaver creating its own tables at runtime would be rule 4 broken by a dependency rather than by a person, which is worse because nobody reviews it - so MemorySaver until a reviewed migration lands. Two follow-ups are owed: delete baseline.py when core/retrieve/ implements the ports, and migrate the checkpoint tables.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0007 - the graph ships before retrieval and before a checkpoint table

nodes.label: Retrieval is a port, not an import
nodes.rationale: core/graph/ports.py declares Passage, Retriever and Reranker; the graph depends only on those, core/retrieve/ implements them when it lands, and scripts/ask.py changes by two import lines. The stopgap lives in Lane A's own directory, labelled disposable and deliberately naive, so nobody mistakes it for Lane B's baseline - which is a measurement committed under eval/results/ with the corpus manifest it ran against.
nodes.norm_label: retrieval is a port, not an import

nodes.label: ADR 0008 - Ingestion runs on a Celery worker
nodes.rationale: The whole pipeline ran on the thread that noticed the file, so a person dropping five scans watched the fifth wait forty seconds. Registration (one hash, one upsert) stays on the capture thread so the filed line appears immediately and the already-indexed check keeps saving work; reading moves behind the queue. Concurrency is one because Ollama is one endpoint in front of one graphics card - the queue buys a free watcher and restart survival, not parallelism, and the demonstration should not claim otherwise. No broker means inline, loudly, because a quiet fallback is the old stall with nobody knowing why.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0008 - ingestion runs on a celery worker

nodes.label: The queue carries a digest, not the document
nodes.rationale: The message is {document_id, digest, mime, original_name} and the worker finds the file again by hashing the inbox. A broker holding 64 MB messages falls over the day somebody scans a folder of photographs, and v1 keeps the inbox as the document store so sending the bytes would be the only copy in the system. A path was rejected: it is a guess the moment somebody tidies their folder, while the SHA-256 is what the documents row is keyed on. Tasks are acks_late with reject_on_worker_lost because the pipeline is idempotent on the hash and losing a document is worse than reading one twice.
nodes.norm_label: the queue carries a digest, not the document

nodes.label: ADR 0009 - next-themes and lucide-react are the only two web dependencies beyond the stack
nodes.rationale: shadcn/ui is not a package but components copied in, several of which import things - so installing shadcn and installing nothing else are not the same act, and pretending otherwise puts undeclared packages in package.json under cover of a rule meant to prevent that. next-themes must write a class onto <html> before first paint or every load of a dark screen flashes white, which is a failure that shows up as a white flash rather than a test failure. clsx, tailwind-merge and cva are not on the list because shadcn's own init generates cn(). The larger cost this record makes visible: 'shadcn/ui' in AGENTS.md under-specifies the web lane.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0009 - next-themes and lucide-react are the only two web dependencies beyond the stack

nodes.label: ADR 0010 - main is unprotected, and the discipline is human
nodes.rationale: GitHub does not enforce rulesets on a private repository on a personal free plan, so a saved ruleset renders on the settings page and merges land unchecked anyway. This was not theoretical: two corpus commits landed directly on main, unreviewed, carrying a batch with no register - the precise class of problem CODEOWNERS was meant to route. A saved-but-inert ruleset is worse than an empty settings page because it tells the next person a gate exists. The task whose Done when can never become true is removed, because a permanent false red trains the team to ignore the board. The weekly integration pass is no longer a tidy-up; it is the only control.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0010 - main is unprotected, and the discipline is human

nodes.label: ADR 0011: The household is people and aliases, and the owner is one of them
nodes.rationale: Citation alone cannot catch an answer about the wrong person: the passage supports the sentence, so the grounding gate passes a confidently wrong answer the moment a second person's paperwork is in the vault.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0011: the household is people and aliases, and the owner is one of them

nodes.label: person_aliases (every printed string resolving to a person)
nodes.rationale: Documents print the same man three ways (MARCUS LIM JUN WEI, Lim Jun Wei Marcus, M. J. W. Lim); knowing the owner's name is not enough, the names have to be reconciled.
nodes.norm_label: person_aliases (every printed string resolving to a person)

nodes.label: facts.subject keeps the unnormalised printed string
nodes.rationale: Mapping at query time instead of backfilling keeps the audit trail honest: a later roster correction cannot retroactively edit what was on the page.
nodes.norm_label: facts.subject keeps the unnormalised printed string

nodes.label: The roster is derived from documents, then confirmed
nodes.rationale: A setup form asks a person to type names from memory before any document is filed, with no feedback about whether what they typed matches what their documents say - and the match is the only thing that matters.
nodes.norm_label: the roster is derived from documents, then confirmed

nodes.label: The model proposes, the person disposes (unconfirmed aliases)
nodes.rationale: The resolver ignores unconfirmed aliases when scoping, so a wrong guess costs a tap rather than a wrong answer.
nodes.norm_label: the model proposes, the person disposes (unconfirmed aliases)

nodes.label: Three buckets: owner, another person, and no subject at all
nodes.rationale: Two buckets would silently break 'my home insurance' - household-level documents belong to nobody in particular - and it would break quietly, the worst way.
nodes.norm_label: three buckets: owner, another person, and no subject at all

nodes.label: Not finding you is an answer (first-person abstention)
nodes.rationale: Saying 'you have no term life policy filed; there is one for Rachel' is more use than a number, and is the difference between honesty about people and mere confidence.
nodes.norm_label: not finding you is an answer (first-person abstention)

nodes.label: A resolved person is shown as a chip, like a citation
nodes.rationale: The defence against being wrong is showing your working, not being careful; a wrong alias should be visible on the screen that used it.
nodes.norm_label: a resolved person is shown as a chip, like a citation

nodes.label: The owner is a row, not a config value baked at install
nodes.rationale: Households are handed over - a daughter takes over her father's paperwork - and an install that cannot follow that gets abandoned rather than corrected.
nodes.norm_label: the owner is a row, not a config value baked at install

nodes.label: Telegram chat_id maps to a person
nodes.rationale: Mapping a chat to a person means a document's owner is known at capture, before parsing, which beats anything inferable from the page and costs one table.
nodes.norm_label: telegram chat_id maps to a person

nodes.label: ADR 0012: Chunks follow the document's headings, and embeddings use the model's task prompts
nodes.rationale: Three ingestion faults sat in front of the retriever: character-count chunking mid-word, tab-separated text, and EmbeddingGemma used without its task prompts. A clause cut in two is retrieved by neither half.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0012: chunks follow the document's headings, and embeddings use the model's task prompts

nodes.label: Chunks follow the document's structure (Docling heading labels)
nodes.rationale: A heading starts a chunk and names every chunk under it; items and table rows pack whole to 900 characters, a longer item splits at sentence ends, a heading-only chunk is not kept.
nodes.norm_label: chunks follow the document's structure (docling heading labels)

nodes.label: Context prefix: title - type - heading - page
nodes.rationale: The title comes from the document's string fields in the pack's declared order, so no field name is written into core/.
nodes.norm_label: context prefix: title - type - heading - page

nodes.label: Task prompts: embed_query and embed_documents
nodes.rationale: EmbeddingGemma was trained with 'task: search result | query:' and 'title: | text:'; without them similarities are lower and flatter. Prompts alone made some questions worse and new chunks alone were worse than both, so they ship as one change.

nodes.label: scripts/reindex.py rebuilds chunks and vectors
nodes.rationale: Both sides must be embedded alike, and re-extraction on a CPU is minutes per document for facts that did not change.

nodes.label: rag_probe2 before/after similarity table (six policies, 13 September)
nodes.norm_label: rag_probe2 before/after similarity table (six policies, 13 september)

nodes.label: Schedule-table questions remain weak (rank 2-4)
nodes.rationale: A table of 'label: value' lines does not look like a question to a dense model; lexical search and a cross-encoder reranker are what read a table.

nodes.label: guardrails.abstain_below was calibrated on un-prompted scores
nodes.rationale: Scores moved up across the board, so the floor wants re-measuring against the golden set rather than keeping.
nodes.norm_label: guardrails.abstain_below was calibrated on un-prompted scores

nodes.label: ADR 0013: A question is understood before it is searched, and scoped before it is cut
nodes.rationale: A person should not have to guess the documents' vocabulary; 'warded', 'kena' and 'can claim?' are how this household talks.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0013: a question is understood before it is searched, and scoped before it is cut

nodes.label: Understand, then search (one model call writes the whole question plus 2-3 document-worded queries)
nodes.rationale: Every phrasing including the person's own words is searched and a passage keeps its best score, so the pack's floor stays a similarity.
nodes.norm_label: understand, then search (one model call writes the whole question plus 2-3 document-worded queries)

nodes.label: The router is unchanged and separate from understanding
nodes.rationale: Folding understanding into the router made 'how much is my pet insurance premium?' a request to act, and wrote weaker search wording.
nodes.norm_label: the router is unchanged and separate from understanding

nodes.label: AskRequest.history carries up to twelve earlier turns
nodes.rationale: History is read only by the understanding step; it is never evidence and cannot be cited.
nodes.norm_label: askrequest.history carries up to twelve earlier turns

nodes.label: Possessive relations scope the question, before the cut to six
nodes.rationale: 'My son's' was left unscoped by design, so an answer about the owner's own whole life policy called the owner 'your son'.
nodes.norm_label: possessive relations scope the question, before the cut to six

nodes.label: The answer prompt carries today's date and names the scoped relation as who the question is about
nodes.norm_label: the answer prompt carries today's date and names the scoped relation as who the question is about

nodes.label: The abstain floor stays at 0.45
nodes.rationale: Lowering it was measured and rejected: the reader answered 'do i have travel insurance?' at 0.38 with 'You have travel insurance.'

nodes.label: A relevance-grading call and an 'answerable' schema flag were both dropped
nodes.rationale: The grader fixed one of five near-misses for 1.4 s; the answerable flag emptied six of eight real answers.
nodes.norm_label: a relevance-grading call and an 'answerable' schema flag were both dropped

nodes.label: Remaining failures are retrieval's to fix (cross-encoder plus lexical)
nodes.rationale: A cross-encoder reads the passage against the question instead of comparing two vectors, and lexical search matches 'car insurance' to a title. The Retriever port is unchanged so they drop in.
nodes.norm_label: remaining failures are retrieval's to fix (cross-encoder plus lexical)

nodes.label: ADR 0014: A pack supplies what the core knows about a domain, and the core stays generic
nodes.rationale: A pack was a field list plus two guardrail numbers: persona.system was read nowhere and grounding was declared but never indexed. The core cannot hold insurance words without breaking the claim that a second pack installs against an unchanged core.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0014: a pack supplies what the core knows about a domain, and the core stays generic

nodes.label: answering.vocabulary: what a household says to what the paper prints
nodes.rationale: 'Warded' is found without the model; only matched lines go into the understanding prompt.
nodes.norm_label: answering.vocabulary: what a household says to what the paper prints

nodes.label: answering.categories: ordered whole-word rules over one printed field
nodes.rationale: A category is derived when a question is asked and never stored, so packs/README.md's 'is it printed?' test still holds; no match is a valid result.
nodes.norm_label: answering.categories: ordered whole-word rules over one printed field

nodes.label: answering.exclusions: headings under which a cover claim is not believed
nodes.rationale: Conservative by design - 'covers emergency dental treatment after an accident' is dropped even though the exception makes it true.
nodes.norm_label: answering.exclusions: headings under which a cover claim is not believed

nodes.label: Inventory: documents on file read from facts with one hand-written query
nodes.norm_label: inventory: documents on file read from facts with one hand-written query

nodes.label: Category filter applied before the keep-6 cut
nodes.rationale: Documents with no category are always kept, so a misfiled product hides rather than deletes.
nodes.norm_label: category filter applied before the keep-6 cut

nodes.label: Code-written absence sentence: 'None of the N policies on file is a dental plan.'
nodes.rationale: ADR 0013 measured a 4B reader writing 'You have travel insurance.' from unrelated passages; a 'no' written by code cannot be talked into a 'yes'.
nodes.norm_label: code-written absence sentence: 'none of the n policies on file is a dental plan.'

nodes.label: The advise route intent returns the pack's advice_decline
nodes.rationale: Guardrails.never_recommends is Literal[True], beside never_acts. Superseded by ADR 0016.
nodes.norm_label: the advise route intent returns the pack's advice_decline

nodes.label: Gate checks beyond citation: printed numbers, exclusion-only claims, sentence cap
nodes.rationale: The number check is literal: a model that reformats 'SGD 1,860.00' as words loses the sentence.
nodes.norm_label: gate checks beyond citation: printed numbers, exclusion-only claims, sentence cap

nodes.label: persona.system is placed before the core's rules, which come last
nodes.norm_label: persona.system is placed before the core's rules, which come last

nodes.label: Published guidance is a second evidence lane, never a second household
nodes.rationale: In documents/ household scoping would treat guidance as belonging to everyone, and 'nothing filed under you' could never fire. One sentence cites one lane, and guidance is cited only after household evidence clears the floor.
nodes.norm_label: published guidance is a second evidence lane, never a second household

nodes.label: Every passage carries a kind: document, inventory or guidance
nodes.norm_label: every passage carries a kind: document, inventory or guidance

nodes.label: ADR 0015: A name scopes a question, and a grandparent is not a parent
nodes.rationale: Two questions reached the reader with other people's documents in them: 'my grandpa's' was not a relation word so nothing scoped it, and 'What is Marcus's premium?' had no 'my' so was not first-person.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0015: a name scopes a question, and a grandparent is not a parent

nodes.label: Grandparent maps to a relation people.relation cannot take, so it abstains
nodes.rationale: Mapping to parent answers from the father's policy; mapping to other answers from whoever was demoted when the household changed hands. Covers grandpa, ah gong, ah ma, popo and variants.
nodes.norm_label: grandparent maps to a relation people.relation cannot take, so it abstains

nodes.label: A member whose display name or confirmed alias is the relation word
nodes.rationale: Applies only when no holder of that relation exists, so a recorded relation always wins over a name. No migration: the roster already says it.
nodes.norm_label: a member whose display name or confirmed alias is the relation word

nodes.label: Naming exactly one person scopes to them (whole name, or a 3+ letter possessive unique to them)
nodes.rationale: 'Lim's' is shared by Marcus and his father so names nobody; 'premium for rachel' is not possessive and is not trusted to be a name. Two people named is left unscoped because a filter would drop the document that answers it.
nodes.norm_label: naming exactly one person scopes to them (whole name, or a 3+ letter possessive unique to them)

nodes.label: Name scoping reuses scope_to, so the three buckets hold
nodes.norm_label: name scoping reuses scope_to, so the three buckets hold

nodes.label: ADR 0016: A pack advises; code calculates from cited facts and reviewed rule values, under recorded consent
nodes.rationale: A 4B generator's arithmetic cannot be trusted and the gate cannot check a figure no page prints; a published rule is a number with a publisher and a date that goes stale. The owner decided a domain pack exists to be a specialist, and a specialist answers 'is my cover enough?'.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0016: a pack advises; code calculates from cited facts and reviewed rule values, under recorded consent

nodes.label: Guardrails.verdict_by_code: a verdict is chosen by code, never written by the model
nodes.rationale: never_recommends is removed; never_acts is unchanged.
nodes.norm_label: guardrails.verdict_by_code: a verdict is chosen by code, never written by the model

nodes.label: PackManifest.advice shapes (gap, remaining_room, keep_or_surrender, compare_own, compare_market, estimate_saving)
nodes.rationale: A closed list rather than a formula language: a formula language would be a runtime query builder in core/, unauditable by a non-programmer.
nodes.norm_label: packmanifest.advice shapes (gap, remaining_room, keep_or_surrender, compare_own, compare_market, estimate_saving)

nodes.label: A grounding corpus lives at packs/<pack>/grounding/<corpus_id>/
nodes.rationale: A pack is a developer-built add-on a household downloads, so its published guidance has to travel with it.
nodes.norm_label: a grounding corpus lives at packs/<pack>/grounding/<corpus_id>/

nodes.label: Rule and market values are typed rows, extracted automatically and approved by a person
nodes.rationale: A value is kept only when its passage is a verbatim substring of the source and its number is a whole printed token; staleness, approval and review are enforced in SQL, not trusted to the author.
nodes.norm_label: rule and market values are typed rows, extracted automatically and approved by a person

nodes.label: modules/advice/ calculators returning a Calculation or a Missing
nodes.rationale: The honest answer to a missing fact is to name it, not to estimate around it - advice on incomplete facts reads as suitability.
nodes.norm_label: modules/advice/ calculators returning a calculation or a missing

nodes.label: Advice graph flow: shape match, subject resolution, consent, AdviceCard, explain
nodes.rationale: The shape is matched from its asked phrases without a model: phrase matching is deterministic and free, and a wrong shape is correct arithmetic on the wrong question.
nodes.norm_label: advice graph flow: shape match, subject resolution, consent, advicecard, explain

nodes.label: Explanation gate: every number equals a printed input, no verdict word, no never_say phrase
nodes.rationale: The role-word check is lexical and can miss a shortfall figure confused with a target.
nodes.norm_label: explanation gate: every number equals a printed input, no verdict word, no never_say phrase

nodes.label: advice_consents, append-only (granted or withdrawn, version, wording hash, channel)
nodes.norm_label: advice_consents, append-only (granted or withdrawn, version, wording hash, channel)

nodes.label: advice_records keeps each answer's full basis
nodes.rationale: Every advice answer can be reconstructed from its record - fact ids, value ids, figures, verdict, disclaimer hash and consent id.
nodes.norm_label: advice_records keeps each answer's full basis

nodes.label: Advice.review: one question runs every shape at once
nodes.rationale: 'What is lacking in my insurance coverage?' asks for every check at once; the verdict is short if any shape is short, still chosen by code.
nodes.norm_label: advice.review: one question runs every shape at once

nodes.label: The adult rule: advice is withheld for a person under 21 or a child with no date of birth on file
nodes.rationale: If two printed dates of birth disagree the later one is used, which errs toward withholding.
nodes.norm_label: the adult rule: advice is withheld for a person under 21 or a child with no date of birth on file

nodes.label: A rider is its own fact, categorised by its own printed name
nodes.norm_label: a rider is its own fact, categorised by its own printed name

nodes.label: ADR 0017: A pack is grounding and persona; the core owns documents
nodes.rationale: Coding agents read ADR 0014 as putting the household's document definitions in packs, so a household's documents belonged to whichever pack happened to be installed and disabling it would switch them off. No pack is the right home for a passport.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0017: a pack is grounding and persona; the core owns documents

nodes.label: A pack holds grounding, persona, guardrails, its own answering and advice - nothing else
nodes.norm_label: a pack holds grounding, persona, guardrails, its own answering and advice - nothing else

nodes.label: core/documents.yaml, the single document catalogue
nodes.rationale: packs.build generates core/document_schemas.py, corpus/register/core_columns.csv, the batch template and docs/field-dictionary.md from it.

nodes.label: Facts are written with pack_id = 'core', and core is always enabled
nodes.rationale: No migration: facts.pack_id stays NOT NULL and holds the constant. Disabling a pack switches off persona, answering, grounding and advice, never documents.
nodes.norm_label: facts are written with pack_id = 'core', and core is always enabled

nodes.label: Two answering layers: core answering always applies, an enabled pack adds to it
nodes.rationale: Vocabulary is unioned; a pack's categories and exclusions name core fields, checked against the catalogue when packs load.
nodes.norm_label: two answering layers: core answering always applies, an enabled pack adds to it

nodes.label: FactInput.pack is removed; doc_types and field are catalogue names
nodes.norm_label: factinput.pack is removed; doc_types and field are catalogue names

nodes.label: Identity data (NRIC/FIN, passport, birth certificate, date of birth) is household data
nodes.rationale: Identity numbers are the most sensitive data in the vault, protected only by on-device storage and the app lock, and need a data-inventory entry before they ship.
nodes.norm_label: identity data (nric/fin, passport, birth certificate, date of birth) is household data

nodes.label: FieldType labelled_money with FieldSpec.repeats
nodes.rationale: One fact row per printed item - value_text the rider name, value_num the amount - so the row holds the pairing and no ALTER is needed behind rule 4.

nodes.label: ADR 0018: The reranker runs in-process, because Ollama cannot serve a cross-encoder
