nodes.norm_label: task: code freeze and tag v1.0-demo

nodes.label: Lane E - Corpus and adversarial testing
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: The input to every other lane, which is why it starts in week 1 and must never become the thing everyone is waiting on.
nodes.norm_label: lane e - corpus and adversarial testing

nodes.label: Register first, documents second
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: Generating documents and working out afterwards what is in them throws away the labels and buys a week of hand-labelling in week 8. Filling the register first gives extraction F1 measured directly, most of golden Set A generated rather than written, and mass production with no code.

nodes.label: The household canon (the Lims of Tampines)
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: One page of facts every document must agree with; one household only, carrying the family tree, the surname convention and the three-policies-on-Marcus table.
nodes.norm_label: the household canon (the lims of tampines)

nodes.label: The document register as ground truth
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: One row per document, one column per field; it exists before the documents do and is what the whole evaluation is scored against.
nodes.norm_label: the document register as ground truth

nodes.label: Register column headings are generated, not chosen
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: If the corpus invented 'period' and the extractor produced 'pay_period' the comparison would silently score zero and the team would hunt a spelling difference for three days, so the possibility was removed rather than documented. A heading that does not make sense is a signal that the field description is unclear - fix Zee's YAML, not the spreadsheet.
nodes.norm_label: register column headings are generated, not chosen

nodes.label: python -m corpus.validate
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: Checks duplicate ids, expiry before start, negative amounts, columns no pack declares, and the same policy number described inconsistently across two documents - the errors that would otherwise surface as a mysterious evaluation result.

nodes.label: Real organisations may be named
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: The invented-organisations rule was withdrawn on 13 September 2026 because a full policy names the hospitals, schemes and dispute bodies a real one names, which is a better retrieval test. The household's own issuers stay the canon's so every document agrees. The SYNTHETIC DOCUMENT footer was dropped: it landed on the last page only and overlapped body text.

nodes.label: batch0-personas is deleted and must not be recreated
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: It held 22 persona sketches spanning three households while the canon holds one, so no subset of it was worth keeping. Sarah Tan Li Ling and Priya Singh were never in the canon; Tan Mei Ling is Marcus's mother and the only Tan in the household.
nodes.norm_label: batch0-personas is deleted and must not be recreated

nodes.label: One document per notebook
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: A single prompt asking for four policies produces four thin documents - the most expensive mistake available here because it is invisible until somebody reads them.

nodes.label: A full policy wording registers as policy_schedule
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: No pack declares 'policy wording', and a doc_type no pack owns goes to quarantine and contributes nothing to facts. The schedule is page 1 and the wordings behind it are chunked for the Ask surface, which is also why field_pages stays empty for these.
nodes.norm_label: a full policy wording registers as policy_schedule

nodes.label: The whole-life expiry_date mismatch
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: policy_schedule marks expiry_date required but a whole life policy has no expiry; the corpus registers maturity at age 100 as a recorded stopgap. The real fix is optional expiry_date or a maturity_date field in Zee's pack.yaml, raised as a decision issue, never patched in the spreadsheet - a field description that does not fit the document will not fit the extractor either.

nodes.label: The synthetic-to-real gap
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: Generated documents are cleaner and more consistent than real ones, so a score measured only on them overstates the system. That is what the 40-document redacted holdout is for: report both numbers and the gap, because the gap is a finding, not a defect.

nodes.label: Batch 4: the deliberately hard documents
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: Faint scans, angled photos, overlapping stamps, two documents on one page - made hard enough to produce an interesting vision-language recovery rate nobody else in the cohort will have.

nodes.label: The 40-document redacted holdout
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: Real documents consented under Siew's protocol, collected in weeks 6-7, existing to measure the overstatement of a synthetic-only score.

nodes.label: Adversarial testing from week 7
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: Stop producing and start attacking; you are looking for a finding, not a bug report. Each attempt is written up as what you tried, what happened, what it means - ten of those is a presentation segment.

nodes.label: Contradiction attack
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: Two documents that disagree on a premium, then a question spanning them. Silently picking one is the finding.

nodes.label: Prompt injection carried inside a document
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: An instruction printed in a document and photographed, to see whether it survives parsing and reaches the model.
nodes.norm_label: prompt injection carried inside a document

nodes.label: Scope attack: asking it to act
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: never_acts is enforced in the manifest; verify it holds in practice and record how the refusal is worded, because a rude refusal is a product problem even when it is a correct one.
nodes.norm_label: scope attack: asking it to act

nodes.label: No code generates corpus documents
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: The agent does the bookkeeping and the substitution, which is where a human makes transcription errors; the notebook does the prose, which is where a script would produce something that reads like a script wrote it.

nodes.label: Task: spot-check 20 register rows against the extractor
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: Each mismatch is written as a question naming the document, the field and both values - e.g. register says 1248.90, extractor says 124890: is the decimal lost in parsing or in the template?
nodes.norm_label: task: spot-check 20 register rows against the extractor

nodes.label: Task: review every quarantined document and label the failure
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: Tagged OCR, layout or schema, feeding the report's honest findings section.
nodes.norm_label: task: review every quarantined document and label the failure

nodes.label: Task: run adversarial Set C and write up the findings
nodes.author: Desmond
nodes.rationale: All 15 items run against the frozen system, with every failure documented rather than quietly fixed.
nodes.norm_label: task: run adversarial set c and write up the findings

nodes.label: Lane C - Governance and assurance
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: Not a documentation lane: six artefacts that are each a chapter of the report, plus the consent protocol that makes the holdout corpus lawful to collect at all. Two of the six are things the technical lanes will not think to ask for until week 8.

nodes.label: Data inventory and flow map
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: What personal data enters, where it rests, what crosses a network boundary - it is the evidence behind the trust-boundary claim in the architecture diagram, and the claim is only defensible if this document exists.

nodes.label: Consent and redaction protocol
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: Governs the 40-document real-document holdout and must exist before Desmond collects anything, not after.

nodes.label: Retention and erasure policy
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: PDPA Protection and Retention Limitation obligations, including the actual erasure path: what DELETE FROM documents cascades to and what it does not.

nodes.label: Model card
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: Model, licence, languages, intended use, out-of-scope use, measured performance, known failure modes; Yew Mun supplies the numbers and the framing is Siew's.

nodes.label: ISO/IEC 22989 to 5338 stage-to-process map
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: Life-cycle stages are 22989 and life-cycle processes are 5338; the map says explicitly which 5338 processes are performed (6.4.7 knowledge acquisition, 6.4.8 AI data engineering, 6.4.14 continuous validation) and which are consciously not.

nodes.label: IMDA mappings and autonomy statement artefact
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: The nine dimensions of the 2024 Model AI Governance Framework for Generative AI and the four of the Agentic AI framework published 22 January 2026.
nodes.norm_label: imda mappings and autonomy statement artefact

nodes.label: The autonomy statement
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: never_acts is not prose but Literal[True] in core/contracts.py, so a pack setting anything else will not load. The system advises; it does not pay, book, renew or file. Under IMDA's agentic framework, pointing at a line of code rather than a paragraph of intent is unusually strong evidence.

nodes.label: Adversarial Set C (15 questions that should not be answered)
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: Requests to act, injection planted in a document, questions about a household member absent from the corpus, invitations to give regulated advice, and answers out of date for the assessment year. Scoring is not accuracy: did it refuse, and was the refusal correctly reasoned and civilly worded.
nodes.norm_label: adversarial set c (15 questions that should not be answered)

nodes.label: Governance claims traced to enforcement points
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: Every fact cites a source because document_id and page are NOT NULL in the migration; the system does not act because never_acts is Literal[True]; no claim without a citation because the answer node refuses an unsupported sentence; nothing leaves the machine because Ollama endpoints are 127.0.0.1. A governance chapter that points at enforcement reads very differently from one that points at policy.
nodes.norm_label: governance claims traced to enforcement points

nodes.label: Say unverified rather than write a plausible sentence
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.rationale: A governance artefact that asserts something the code does not do is worse than one with a gap in it.
nodes.norm_label: say unverified rather than write a plausible sentence

nodes.label: Task: sign off the capture-to-database path against the data inventory
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.norm_label: task: sign off the capture-to-database path against the data inventory

nodes.label: Task: write the PDPA position on using synthetic data
nodes.author: Siew
nodes.norm_label: task: write the pdpa position on using synthetic data

nodes.label: Lane B - Retrieval and evaluation
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Owns the numbers that carry the grade: the report's strongest claim is not that the system works but that it was measured three times and the movement can be explained.

nodes.label: Measurement is owned separately from the engine
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Christian owns the extraction engine, Yew Mun owns its measurement: the person who built a thing should not be the only person scoring it.
nodes.norm_label: measurement is owned separately from the engine

nodes.label: Week 1 hardware benchmark with run-to-run spread
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Every VRAM number in the proposal is a planning estimate; the measured table replaces all of them. A bare median is not comparable across five machines because on a desktop in normal use the between-invocation spread is wider than the within-run spread, so scripts/bench_runtime.py measures it identically everywhere rather than being hand-assembled.
nodes.norm_label: week 1 hardware benchmark with run-to-run spread

nodes.label: The deliberately naive retrieval baseline
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Dense-only pgvector, no reranking, fusion or contextualisation. It is the number everything later is compared against, so it must be honest rather than flattering - a baseline you tuned is not a baseline.

nodes.label: One variable per pull request
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Chunk size, contextualisation prompt, top_k before and after reranking, the abstain floor: each is its own PR with its own numbers, because a PR that changes three things at once has told you nothing about any of them.

nodes.label: Golden Set A - answerable (60)
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Twelve questions each from all five, by end of week 3; every question cites the document and page from Desmond's register, which is what makes the set gradeable without a human in the loop.

nodes.label: Golden Set B - hard negatives (25)
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: The set to care about: the headline result is abstention rate, not accuracy, because a system that declines when its evidence does not cover the question makes a trustworthiness claim an accuracy score cannot make on its behalf. Target 0.95, and the number most likely to disappoint at run 1.

nodes.label: Golden Set C - adversarial (15)
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Prompt injection, contradictory documents, out-of-scope requests; written by Siew.

nodes.label: The nine metrics and their targets
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Context recall 0.85, context precision 0.70, faithfulness 0.90, answer relevancy 0.80, Set B abstention 0.95, extraction F1 0.90, plus decode throughput and peak VRAM measured and reported.
nodes.norm_label: the nine metrics and their targets

nodes.label: The judge model is local
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Served through Ollama's OpenAI-compatible endpoint so no evaluation question leaves the machine - a governance commitment, not a preference, and Siew's data inventory says so.

nodes.label: Committed runs are never deleted
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Every run lives under eval/results/ because the trend across runs is the finding, not any single score.

nodes.label: Task: hybrid retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Done when dense and tsvector rankings are fused so exact policy numbers are findable while paraphrases still work.
nodes.norm_label: task: hybrid retrieval with reciprocal rank fusion

nodes.label: Task: contextualised chunking and the reranker
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Each chunk carries a one-line context prefix and bge-reranker-v2-m3 cuts 40 candidates to 6.
nodes.norm_label: task: contextualised chunking and the reranker

nodes.label: Task: evaluation run 3 plus the holdout run
nodes.author: Yew Mun
nodes.rationale: Three runs in one table plus synthetic versus real scores with the gap stated plainly.
nodes.norm_label: task: evaluation run 3 plus the holdout run

nodes.label: Lane D - Domain packs and interface
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: You do not need to program: you need to know what a document is and what is printed on it, which is the actual scarce skill. The lane runs first because nothing downstream can start until the field names are fixed.
nodes.norm_label: lane d - domain packs and interface

nodes.label: ADR 0017 - a pack is grounding and persona
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: Since 17 September document types and their fields live in core/documents.yaml owned by the core; a pack holds its grounding corpus, persona, guardrails, answering rules and advice. A field Zee wants to name is proposed for core/documents.yaml instead.
nodes.norm_label: adr 0017 - a pack is grounding and persona

nodes.label: pack.yaml is the only file Zee authors
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: schemas.py, the register CSV and docs/field-dictionary.md are generated by packs.build. A field name is written down in exactly one place, which is what stops the pack and the corpus drifting apart - a failure that otherwise surfaces as a silently zero evaluation score in week 8.
nodes.norm_label: pack.yaml is the only file zee authors

nodes.label: Do not rename a field after Desmond has started
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: Free in week 1, expensive in week 6; raise it in the group first.
nodes.norm_label: do not rename a field after desmond has started

nodes.label: Grounding sources must be official issuers
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: IRAS, CPF Board, MAS, MOH, a named regulator, or an industry association for figures it publishes itself (LIA, compareFIRST). Not a blog and never a seller's page; record the retrieval date and Siew reviews provenance.
nodes.norm_label: grounding sources must be official issuers

nodes.label: The four surfaces: Today, Ask, Vault, Packs
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.norm_label: the four surfaces: today, ask, vault, packs

nodes.label: Lock the design tokens before building any screen
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: One accent colour, one radius scale, one type scale: an agent given tokens produces a consistent interface across sessions, and an agent given 'make it look clean' produces four different ones.
nodes.norm_label: lock the design tokens before building any screen

nodes.label: The platform argument: one core, two domains
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: The strongest thing to show is the same core answering two completely different domains because two YAML files were dropped in.
nodes.norm_label: the platform argument: one core, two domains

nodes.label: Task: define the pack catalogue - the nine deferred packs
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: Each deferred pack names its document types, registered modules and grounding corpus against the same manifest, so the expansion story is specified without being built.
nodes.norm_label: task: define the pack catalogue - the nine deferred packs

nodes.label: Task: write the user stories with acceptance criteria
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: One story per persona, each with a testable acceptance criterion the UI is built against.
nodes.norm_label: task: write the user stories with acceptance criteria

nodes.label: PaperBrain
nodes.rationale: A fully local brain for personal paperwork: SQLite on disk, Ollama for embeddings and generation, no API keys, no cloud, no telemetry. Phase 1 is the retrieval layer; facts and reminders tables are already in the schema for what builds on top.

nodes.label: The pb command line
nodes.rationale: pb add / ingest / docs / search / ask, with pb doctor naming exactly what is missing; ingest is re-runnable because unchanged files are skipped by hash, making it a cheap cron job.

nodes.label: PaperBrain hybrid retrieval (BM25 + dense, fused by RRF)
nodes.rationale: BM25 over SQLite FTS5 catches literal tokens like a policy number or an amount; 768-dim nomic-embed-text cosine catches paraphrase. RRF combines them so neither needs a calibrated score.
nodes.norm_label: paperbrain hybrid retrieval (bm25 + dense, fused by rrf)

nodes.label: Exhaustive cosine instead of an ANN index
nodes.rationale: A few tens of thousands of chunks score in milliseconds on this machine, and it avoids a native ANN extension that would complicate every future pip install.
nodes.norm_label: exhaustive cosine instead of an ann index

nodes.label: PaperBrain privacy boundary
nodes.rationale: The only network call is to 127.0.0.1:11434; the database lives at ~/.paperbrain/paperbrain.db and deleting it forgets everything; original files are never modified or moved; .gitignore excludes *.db.

nodes.label: PaperBrain dependency set
nodes.rationale: numpy and pypdf are required; python-docx, pytesseract, pdf2image, Pillow and pillow-heif are recommended and carry the OCR and .HEIC paths, which also need the tesseract and poppler system binaries.

nodes.label: Constraint: fully offline
nodes.rationale: Personal paperwork is the most sensitive data most people own, so no embeddings API, no hosted vector store, no crash reporter. Together with running on one laptop and surviving three months of neglect, this rules out Docker, Postgres/pgvector, Chroma and a LangChain layer that breaks on upgrade.

nodes.label: SQLite for everything
nodes.rationale: Documents, chunks, the FTS5 index and the vectors live in one file that can be copied, backed up by Time Machine or deleted to forget everything; FTS5 ships with macOS and Python so keyword search costs zero dependencies.

nodes.label: Vectors as BLOBs, scored in numpy
nodes.rationale: Embeddings are L2-normalised at write time so cosine is one matrix-vector product; 20k chunks is a 60 MB float32 matrix scored in milliseconds. ANN indexes only pay off orders of magnitude beyond a household's paperwork and each is a native wheel that can break on an OS upgrade - revisit past ~200k chunks.
nodes.norm_label: vectors as blobs, scored in numpy

nodes.label: Hybrid retrieval, not embeddings alone
nodes.rationale: Half of all paperwork questions hinge on an exact string - a policy number, an amount, a vendor - and embedding models smear those. BM25 nails them nearly free, and RRF fuses the rankings without needing the two scores on the same scale.

nodes.label: OCR is per page, not per file
nodes.rationale: A 30-page policy usually has 29 text pages and one scanned signature page; rasterising the whole document would be slow and would lose quality on pages that already have perfect text, so only pages with no text layer are OCR'd.
nodes.norm_label: ocr is per page, not per file

nodes.label: Hash-based idempotency
nodes.rationale: A file whose sha256 matches what is stored is skipped before extraction, which makes ingest safe to schedule and makes 're-index everything' a normal operation rather than a scary one.

nodes.label: Chunking respects paragraphs
nodes.rationale: A receipt's line items and a policy's clause must not be cut mid-item or retrieval returns half an amount; splits happen at blank lines first, with a hard character cut only inside an unusually long paragraph and a 200-char stitch from the previous chunk.

nodes.label: The prompt refuses to guess
nodes.rationale: For paperwork a confidently invented renewal date is worse than 'I don't have that document', so the system prompt forbids outside knowledge, requires [n] citations and requires verbatim figures.

nodes.label: PaperBrain handled failure modes
nodes.rationale: Ollama down raises OllamaUnavailable with the exact fix while ingest still stores text; missing tesseract/poppler still ingests text-layer PDFs; a swapped embedding model is caught by dimension mismatch and BM25 carries the query; a modified file is replaced atomically.

nodes.label: The facts table as an extension point
nodes.rationale: Structured extraction lands here with each row pointing back at the chunk it came from, so nothing is unverifiable; doc_type and doc_date are regex heuristics a pb classify pass can upgrade without touching the schema.
nodes.norm_label: the facts table as an extension point

nodes.label: The reminders table as an extension point
nodes.rationale: Keeping it in the same database means a reminder can always be traced back to its source document.
nodes.norm_label: the reminders table as an extension point

nodes.label: Roadmap phase 1 - retrieval
nodes.rationale: Done apart from a watch mode and a ~30-question eval set, so retrieval changes can be measured instead of vibed.

nodes.label: Roadmap phase 2 - facts
nodes.rationale: Turn documents into rows with a strict JSON schema per document type, every row pointing back at its source chunk: no fact without a chunk id.

nodes.label: Roadmap phase 3 - reminders
nodes.rationale: Reminders derived from facts with a per-type lead time, surfaced via pb agenda, macOS notifications and an optional local .ics export - still no cloud - with dismiss, snooze and done so it stops nagging.

nodes.label: Roadmap phase 4 - agent
nodes.rationale: Only after facts and reminders are trustworthy: a tool-using loop over the local model handling multi-step questions that need two facts and a comparison rather than one retrieval.

nodes.label: Explicitly not doing: cloud, hosted vectors, autonomous spending
nodes.rationale: No cloud sync or mobile app because the threat model is the whole point; no hosted vector database; no autonomous actions that spend money or send mail - it drafts, you send.
nodes.norm_label: explicitly not doing: cloud, hosted vectors, autonomous spending

nodes.label: Sample home contents insurance policy
nodes.rationale: Carries an exact policy number (AIA-HC-7741928), a renewal date and a water-damage clause - the paraphrase-versus-literal-token pair the hybrid retrieval design exists to serve.

nodes.label: Sample supermarket tax invoice
nodes.rationale: A GST line and an amount paid, which is the spend-by-month question phase 2 is meant to answer from facts rather than prose.

nodes.label: Sample school term notice
nodes.rationale: Carries a consent-form deadline, the kind of dated obligation the reminders phase derives a lead time from.

nodes.label: web/ - the PARROT interface
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: Next.js 15 App Router, Tailwind, shadcn/ui and AI SDK useChat; the resolved interface is the Kitchen Table canvas, whose artboard 1o is the handoff with every token value, the font pairing and a file-by-file list of what changes.

nodes.label: Today surface
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: What the assistant wants to tell you before you ask - reminders and alerts - which is what makes it feel alive rather than like a search box.

nodes.label: Ask surface
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: The conversation with inline citations: every factual sentence links to a document and page.

nodes.label: Vault surface
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: Everything filed, including the quarantine queue rendered as 'needs your eyes' rather than hidden in a log.

nodes.label: Packs surface
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: What the assistant knows about and what it could know about - where the expansion story becomes visible to a user.

nodes.label: Terracotta is intent, evergreen is evidence
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: --brand marks intent (wordmark, current tab, primary action); --accent marks evidence only (source chip, verified field, a switch that is on). If it is green there is a document behind it, so a screen that spends green on a button has taken the one signal this product runs on and made it decoration.
nodes.norm_label: terracotta is intent, evergreen is evidence

nodes.label: Login is a local passphrase
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: An offline-capable assistant that needs a network to open is not offline-capable, so federated identity is out; Google OAuth appears only for Drive authorisation, post-MVP.

nodes.label: Empty and error states are the deliverable
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: A screen that only looks right with fixture data is not done.
nodes.norm_label: empty and error states are the deliverable

nodes.label: PARROT holds exactly one household
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: A vault containing two families has two people called 'my father', two sets of policy numbers and no correct answer to a question about either - the tool is corrupted rather than merely untidy. The household is the Lims of Tampines and every name in the file is one of those five.

nodes.label: A persona is a role inside the household, not a separate customer
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: The design pack's five outsiders would break the one-household rule, so each story is recast onto the Lim who holds the documents it needs. Marcus carries three of five because he holds nineteen of thirty documents in batch1, which is more honest than inventing people to spread the stories evenly.
nodes.norm_label: a persona is a role inside the household, not a separate customer

nodes.label: Every criterion binds to a register row and a supplied date
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: 'An answer with a citation' is untestable; 'names Lionhead Life Assurance and cites b1-0008' is a test. /today takes ?as_of= which moves the whole reminder sweep rather than the heading, which is also how the demonstration opens a lead window without editing a database.
nodes.norm_label: every criterion binds to a register row and a supplied date

nodes.label: Rachel - Reminder module on Today
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: Reading the screen must never write: /api/today is a GET sweeping with mark=False so a second load is identical, and only the nightly Celery pass writes last_notified_at. URGENT_WITHIN_DAYS = 30 is the only ordering decision the screen makes because urgency arrives already sorted.

nodes.label: Marcus - retrieval core on Ask
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: A claim whose chunk_ids is empty is not rendered at all: an uncited sentence reaching the screen is a defect, not a formatting problem. The same whole-life policy is described three times in the corpus specifically to catch a system that answers from whichever document it found first.

nodes.label: Abstention is a designed screen
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: A question no document covers returns kind: abstention in its own visually distinct state showing what is missing rather than a hedged guess, and it must not be styled as an error. A request to act returns kind: refusal with the pack disclaimer - never_acts is enforced in contracts, the interface only shows the boundary.

nodes.label: Marcus and Rachel - capture into the Vault
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: One row per SHA-256 content key however many times it is captured; anything that fails to parse or extracts below confidence lands in 'needs your eyes' with a quarantine_reason so nothing disappears silently; a phone photograph of a scanned page is the realistic worst case rather than the exception.
nodes.norm_label: marcus and rachel - capture into the vault

nodes.label: Marcus - Alert module on Today (SRS ceiling)
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: The alert states both the figure reached and the ceiling because the reader has to be told where they stand; it debounces at 168 hours since a threshold crossing is news once a week; and the ceiling is per person, because a household tool that summed two people's contributions would warn them both wrongly.
nodes.norm_label: marcus - alert module on today (srs ceiling)

nodes.label: The household ledger - specified, not built in v1
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: iras_tax registers tracker metrics and PackSummary.tracker is already on the Packs surface, but modules/ holds only reminder and alert, so there is nothing for the interface to render. Writing that down is the point; building it is Lane A's, needs a manifest against TrackerConfig, and should be an ADR before a pull request.
nodes.norm_label: the household ledger - specified, not built in v1

nodes.label: Open question: two directories still contain other families
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: batch0-personas holds a Tan family and Priya Singh alongside the Lims; its README says it is a mood board that must never be loaded, but a mood board introducing four more households is exactly what the one-household rule exists to prevent, and somebody will eventually load it for the demo.
nodes.norm_label: open question: two directories still contain other families

nodes.label: Open question: snooze and dismiss are not in the contract
nodes.author: Zee
nodes.rationale: TodayItem has no field for that state and /api/today deliberately sweeps with mark=False so reading never writes; making it real is a core/contracts.py change and therefore its own reviewed pull request, so the criterion is written without it.
nodes.norm_label: open question: snooze and dismiss are not in the contract

nodes.label: Open question: the tax payment due date never fires a reminder
